name: Central Luzon
summary_text: Angeles City and the Clark-Subic corridor in Pampanga constitute the region's principal traveler-facing risk. In June 2025 the National Bureau of Investigation's Bataan District Office dismantled a trafficking operation at Field Sensation's Bar in Angeles City, arresting four people and rescuing 45 victims including 13 minors; in March 2025 the same office arrested a foreign national and accomplices in Angeles City under the Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act, rescuing 12 victims including 5 minors. Peer-reviewed research describes the US military-basing economy around Clark as sustaining sexual markets that disproportionately exploit poor transgender Filipina women, and the 2024 US Trafficking in Persons Report confirms traffickers exploit victims in tourist destinations and urban areas around the country. For a transgender visitor the exposure is two-fold: the venues where trans women are concentrated in commercial sex work carry the highest violence and trafficking risk, and enforcement sweeps can sweep up anyone in the vicinity. No protective ordinance cluster comparable to the capital region or Central Visayas is documented here.
